Michele — thanks for the clear asks. Put together a concise MAP and attached an initial capacity worksheet (BridgeScale_MAP_capacity_v1.xlsx). High-level notes in-line below, and next steps at the bottom.

1) Lead times (typical, subject to procurement & supplier windows):
   - H100 (Dedicated/private): 12–16 weeks from order to delivery.
   - A100 (Dedicated): 6–10 weeks.
   - For Private/on-prem we add 2–4 weeks for on-site validation and networking (varies by customer firewall/KMS setup).

2) Right-size recommendation (for pilot -> production ramp):
   - Pilot (2-week eval): 2x A100-equivalent instances with 64GB memory — this covers latency-sensitive sampling at the sample rate you described.
   - Production baseline: 6–8 A100-equivalent slots for 50 req/s, 8k median tokens, with autoscale headroom to 12.
   - Private/latency-critical: suggest starting with 4 H100-equivalents if you need deterministic p99 latency and more KV cache capacity.

3) Escape hatch options (to mitigate long lead times):
   - Short-term: Redwood Hosted burst pool (shared capacity) — available within 48 hours, lower commitment, slightly higher unit cost.
   - Medium-term: Dedicated reserved tranche with staggered delivery (we can reserve 40% immediately, remainder on 8–12 week cadence).
   - Long-term: On-prem staging lane — containerized runtime we ship for air-gap validation; full private roll in 2–4 weeks after acceptance.

4) MAP milestones (attached sheet has dates you can edit):
   - 06/30: MAP sign-off (agreement on sizes and milestone owner)
   - 07/05–07/18: Pilot eval (two-week test window)
   - 07/20–08/10: Procurement & SOC2 evidence handoff
   - 08/15: Initial tranche delivered (if ordering A100s this week)

Next steps: please review the attached MAP and the H100 lead times sheet (H100_leadtimes_sheet.csv). If this looks good, we will push DocuSign for the initial tranche and open the Hosted burst pool as an escape hatch during procurement.

Attachments: BridgeScale_MAP_capacity_v1.xlsx, H100_leadtimes_sheet.csv

Best,
